Definition: Integration of statistics, census data, administrative data for planning, M&E, and evidence-based policymaking
Comments: No documented national statistics integration with data exchange. UNDP scores show very limited digital government capacity overall.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown understated documented activity. An AfDB project-progress report (2026) shows Eritrea's National Statistics Office (NSO) has established its own data centre, migrated datasets to modern servers, and piloted an Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) across three ministries (Finance/National Development, Agriculture, Education) producing reconciled reports; a UNDP news item (2026) and UNFPA case study (2025) confirm the NSO is collecting secondary administrative data from line ministries to compile national accounts and conducted a large digitally-collected household survey (EPHS 2025). However, no formal, government-wide data exchange or interoperability framework exists (Global Digital Identity Index, 2022), so this is project-based sectoral data-sharing rather than integration through a central exchange. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Under development); flagged for human review because the correct code depends on how strictly 'data exchange' is interpreted against these bespoke administrative data flows.
revised_comments: Eritrea's National Statistics Office (NSO) has, since 2020, been building administrative data-sharing capacity through the EU/UNDP-supported Strengthening of Eritrea's National Statistics and Macroeconomic Statistics Systems (SENSS) programme and an AfDB-funded public financial management project. The NSO has established its own data centre and IT infrastructure, migrated its datasets to modern servers, and now collects secondary administrative data from line ministries (including the Ministry of Finance and National Development, Agriculture, and Education) to compile national accounts and reconciled financial reports through pilot use of an Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS). In 2025 the NSO also completed a large national household survey (EPHS 2025) using digital data-collection tools. These are sector-specific and project-based data flows rather than a formal, government-wide data exchange platform, and no national interoperability framework exists; administrative data integration for planning purposes is accordingly assessed as under development.
